title: Express Board and published-read test intent through page objects

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage — SEED-300 "Express Board test intent through page objects"

Verdict: Caught.

Story and revision: .planning/seeds/SEED-300-dashboard-test-page-objects.md#express-board-test-intent-through-page-objects (Key example 4 / "Story inspection and references" finding); plan .planning/slice-plans/584-board-test-intent/PLAN.md; revision a087385504bfb086cdfafaeae961aa478e5bd948, checked in an isolated detached scratch worktree (job tmp ic-scratch, npm ci), never the execution checkout.

Promise: A Done reference is pending (its record held); the reader presses Inspect story and the held answer arrives before pointer release. The arriving destination must not take focus; the pressed action keeps focus, and pointer-up opens "Detail for Story A" and focuses Hide detail.

Fault (product side, as suggested, validated against the revision): dashboard/src/storyNavigation.tsx, the pending-journey give-up effect. Both calls `untilOwnMove(giveUp, isStoryReferenceAction)` and `range.givenUpOnOwnMove(journey.demand, giveUp, isStoryReferenceAction)` were changed to except `(event) => event.type === "pointerdown" || isStoryReferenceAction(event)`. A pointer-down therefore no longer cancels the pending jump or its Recently done demand, and the arrival reveals and focuses the destination. Fixtures and assertions were not changed.

Maintained check: dashboard/tests/navigation/story-reference-done-cancellation.spec.ts:73, "pointer down stops a pending Done jump while its data arrives and the pointer's chosen action still clicks" (with pointerDownOn in dashboard/tests/storyCardControls.ts).

Commands (from the scratch checkout):
env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES caffeinate -s -i npm run test:dashboard -- dashboard/tests/navigation/story-reference-done-cancellation.spec.ts --workers=1 --reporter=list
The witness used the same command with the scratch spec dashboard/tests/navigation/zz-ic-witness.spec.ts.

Evidence:
- Baseline (load averages 10.48 / 21.77 / 24.13): all 3 tests passed in 16.2s; the target test passed in 2.7s. The scratch tree was clean (0 porcelain entries) before the probe.
- Independent witness. This unmaintained scratch spec followed the same journey and only logged document.activeElement. On baseline: Inspect story held focus after arrival, the destination was not focused, and after pointer-up Hide detail had focus with 1 detail region. Under the fault: after arrival, with the pointer still down, focus was on the ARTICLE for SEED-227#progressive-27 (destination focused: true). After pointer-up, focus stayed on that article and the detail region count was 0, so the pressed Inspect story action was lost. The wrong behavior was observed on the intended path.
- Faulted maintained run (load averages 8.04 / 19.54 / 23.18): 2 failed, 1 passed, 20.9s. The target test failed at L84, `await expect(destination).not.toBeFocused()`, with Received: focused on `[data-done-story="SEED-227#progressive-27"]`. That is the assertion that caught the fault. The neighbouring test at L43 ("a developer's later move or latest-ten choice supersedes a pending Done reference") also failed, at L53 `expect(referenceNotice(page)).toBeEmpty()`, because the click's pointer-down no longer superseded the journey. The Tab test at L96 still passed, as expected for a keyboard path.
- Claim boundary: this covers only the pointer-down-before-arrival path on a Done reference whose record is held.

Restoration: An EXIT/INT/TERM trap ran `git checkout -- dashboard/src/storyNavigation.tsx`, and I deleted the witness spec. After that the scratch tree had 0 porcelain entries and `git diff --quiet HEAD` passed at a087385504bfb086cdfafaeae961aa478e5bd948. I reran the same command (load averages 11.88 / 18.74 / 22.67): 3 passed in 19.7s, target test 3.1s. I then removed the scratch worktree with `git worktree remove --force`, and it no longer appears in `git worktree list`. I did not touch the stash stack. The execution checkout is still at a0873855 with one modification I did not make (.planning/seeds/SEED-300-dashboard-test-page-objects.md, presumably the caller's wrap-up edit), which I left as it was.

Next proof action: None needed for this promise. The maintained assertion at L84 catches the product fault on the observed path.

Prior disposition: Execution's earlier test-side fault (dropping mouse.down in pointerDownOn) is a separate check. This probe adds a product-side catch and makes no new repair decision.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, Playwright list reporter wall totals): baseline 16.2s, faulted 20.9s, restored 19.7s, witness 7.1s baseline + 12.0s faulted. That is about 76s in all, at external load averages of about 8–12 (1-minute).
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part during the probe.
- Agent effort: unavailable as a separately supported measure. There is no token or tool-time accounting I can observe. About 20 tool calls were made (counted, not timed).

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 189150 ms (measured), from 1794537381000 to 1794537570150 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

---

Wrap-up disposition (2026-11-13)
- Checked revision: a087385504bfb086cdfafaeae961aa478e5bd948 (execution-complete record; product and test code identical to 974e2b7f).
- Evidence: maintained assertion story-reference-done-cancellation.spec.ts:84 failed on the independently witnessed product fault; restoration verified.
- Decision: no action. The verdict is Caught; no gap needs a follow-up. This one probe covers only the pointer-down-before-arrival path on a held Done reference, not the whole story.
- Canonical follow-up links: none.
